A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Coarse-Grained Boltzmann Generators by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and CG-BG evaluations on the Müller–Brown potential and alanine dipeptide, including accuracy, runtime, and clipping experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original CG-BG evaluations on the retained systems and on alanine tripeptide and hexapeptide, with quantitative results and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The ESFM-trained PMF, flow-matching proposal, importance reweighting, and 1% clipping procedure remain unchanged, as do the specified network architectures and Appendix F algorithms. Appendix C newly documents center-of-mass centering and noise, without establishing that this was a newly introduced procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds alanine tripeptide (42 atoms) and hexapeptide (72 atoms), extending molecular complexity beyond the retained Müller–Brown and 22-atom dipeptide systems. Tripeptide uses both CG mappings and hexapeptide uses Core Beta; evaluation focuses on selected dihedral pairs.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds TarFlow and ECNF++ to the dipeptide accuracy/ESS comparison against the explicit-solvent reference. v1 compared accuracy with generalized Born baselines and included ECNF++ only in a runtime comparison. The new caption attributes the atomistic BG results to prior studies; it does not establish new baseline training.

E3.justification: Appendices C–D revise MB flow training from 2000 to 1000 epochs, dipeptide training batch size from 256 to 1024, ODE tolerances from 1e-4 to 1e-5, and PMF training from 250 to 300 epochs with changed decay and final-checkpoint selection. New peptide experiments introduce longer trajectories and targeted biasing protocols. Appendix B also replaces the stated implicit-solvent 2 fs/H-bond constraints with a blanket 0.5 fs/unconstrained setting. These are reported protocol revisions, not proof of reruns.

E4.justification: The clipping analysis expands from dipeptide to tripeptide and hexapeptide, with separate ablation tables and sensitivity curves for five system/mapping combinations (v2 Tables 7–9 and Figure 10). Resolution comparisons and structural diagnostics also extend to larger peptides. The short 10 ns unbiased-dipeptide sampling-failure illustration in v1 Figure 6b is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report uncertainty values and specify ten independent MB data-generation trajectories. v2 changes table notation from ± values to parenthetical digits, but introduces no stated uncertainty-estimation procedure, model-run count, confidence interval, or significance test. The origins of the reported uncertainties remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised and expanded. In Table 2, Heavy Atom dipeptide JS/PMF/ESS changes from 0.0075/0.2493/0.2325 to 0.0048/0.2005/0.5112. Unclipped dipeptide ESS changes from near-zero or unavailable values in v1 Table 6 to approximately 0.36–0.46 in v2 Table 7. Runtime values change, and larger-peptide and atomistic-baseline results are added. Changed protocols prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equation (18) adds the 1/B normalization and explicitly defines ESS as a fraction in (0,1], correcting the mathematical definition to match fractional reporting. Propositions 1–3 and the Appendix A proofs are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the claim that this is the first BG formulation incorporating machine-learning potentials as importance-sampling target energies. The main contributions—CG sampling, ESFM-based PMF learning, solvent-mediated accuracy, and computational savings—are otherwise retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 explicitly acknowledges learned-PMF approximation bias. Appendix B qualifies larger-peptide convergence as primarily covering the targeted dihedrals, and Table 5 cautions about cross-paper runtime comparability. Section 4.2 adds an interpretation of coarser mappings as improving ESS while generally reducing reweighted accuracy.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D substantially expand experimental documentation with larger-peptide simulation recipes, explicit flow/PMF training sample counts, and center-of-mass preprocessing. Hyperparameters and checkpoint-selection instructions are revised. Some earlier reproducibility information is removed, including the dipeptide box size and trajectory-recording stride; hardware, software, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds constrained mean-force approaches and newer generative-sampling references, while explaining the relationship to already-cited Tamagnone et al. (2024) and Kohler et al. (2023). Future-work citations expand and the first-formulation novelty claim is removed, but the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method exposition, simulation-free evaluation discussion, related work, and future-work paragraphs undergo extensive rewriting. Appendix G is reorganized around the expanded systems and analyses. These changes substantially revise the narrative and explanations while retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively redrawn and regrouped: v1 Figures 3–4 become v2 Figure 2, the MB figure moves to Appendix G, and Ramachandran panels are consolidated and promoted into the main text. Dataset, runtime, and ablation tables expand across peptides. A new labeling inconsistency appears in v2 Figure 11, whose axes say phi despite its psi caption.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its scalability argument mainly with a toy potential and dipeptide. The larger-peptide evaluations, direct atomistic-BG accuracy comparisons, and expanded resolution/clipping analyses substantially strengthen evidence for the central claims. Explicit PMF-bias and targeted-dihedral qualifications improve their interpretation. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: larger-system validation remains limited to selected dihedrals, and Appendix G.4 retains blanket clipping-benefit statements that conflict with the revised dipeptide results in Table 7.
